verses.text: After all this, the officials came to me and said, “The people of Israel, the priests, and the Levites haven’t kept apart from the peoples of the lands. They’ve followed the detestable practices of the Canaanites, Hittites, Perizzites, Jebusites, Ammonites, Moabites, Egyptians, and Amorites.

They’ve taken daughters from those peoples as wives for themselves and their sons, so the descendants set apart for God have mixed with the peoples of the lands. The officials and rulers have led the way in this wrong.”
When I heard that, I tore my clothes and my robe, pulled hair from my head and beard, and sat down in shock.
Everyone who trembled at the words of the God of Israel gathered around me because of what the returned exiles had done. I sat there stunned until the evening offering.
At the evening offering, I got up from where I’d been sitting in humiliation, with my clothes and robe still torn. I dropped to my knees and held out my hands to the LORD my God.
I said, “My God, I’m too ashamed and embarrassed to lift my face to you. Our wrongdoing has piled up over our heads, and our guilt reaches all the way to heaven.

We’ve been deeply guilty from our ancestors’ days right up to today. Because of our wrongdoing, we, our kings, and our priests were handed over to the kings of other lands, to the sword, exile, plunder, and public shame. That’s where we are today.

But now, for this brief moment, the LORD our God has shown us grace. He’s let some of us escape and given us a foothold in his holy place, so our God can brighten our eyes and give us a little new life in our bondage.

We’re still in bondage, but our God hasn’t abandoned us there. He’s shown us faithful love in the sight of the Persian kings, giving us new life so we can raise up our God’s house, rebuild its ruins, and have a wall in Judah and Jerusalem.
“And now, our God, what can we say after all this? We walked away from your commands,

the ones you gave through your servants the prophets: ‘The land you’re going to take possession of is unclean because of the peoples who live there. Their detestable practices have filled it from one end to the other with uncleanness.

So don’t give your daughters to their sons or take their daughters for your sons. Don’t ever seek their peace or prosperity. Then you can stay strong, enjoy what the land produces, and leave it to your children as their inheritance forever.’
“After everything that’s happened to us for the evil we did and the guilt we brought on ourselves, you, our God, have punished us less than we deserved and let this group survive.
Are we really going to break your commands again and join ourselves to the peoples who do these detestable things? Wouldn’t you be angry enough to wipe us out, with no one left and nobody escaping?
LORD, God of Israel, you’re righteous. Some of us have escaped and are still here today. Here we stand before you with all our guilt, though no one can stand before you because of it.”
